decision: Not promoted to the default path. The T16 consumer is bit-exact on every measured shape, but under the interleaved paired protocol it is 0.773-0.803x on the wide-N shapes and 0.633x at K=5120/N=5120. Those ranges top out below 1.0 (max 0.962, 0.911, 0.883, 1.844), so the wide-N deficit is a real effect and not drift. The one narrow-N shape (N=2048) has a median of 1.044 but spans 0.857-2.219, which is too wide to call a win. Halving payload bytes does not help where the raw owner already saturates the machine; the duplicate 8-byte window reads it performs are L1 hits, so both owners issue the same number of load requests and the T16 path only adds header work and register pressure. The wide-header variant narrowed the deficit but did not flip it.

not_measured.real_ud_tensor_rates: the per-tensor rates use synthetic payload bytes, not the 117 resident UD-Q4_K_M IQ4_XS tensors
not_measured.wide_header_loads: the variant that reads d/hi/lo for eight columns as contiguous u32 vectors (16 loads instead of 24) is not implemented

protocol.method: interleaved paired rounds: both owners timed back to back inside one process, 40 launches per round, 15 rounds after 8 warmup pairs
protocol.reported: median per-launch ms per owner, and the median/min/max of the per-round raw/T16 ratio
protocol.shape: synthetic IQ4_XS bytes, d forced to f16 1.0, random payload

superseded.reason: The first version of this artifact reported a sequential A-then-B protocol. Re-running unchanged raw-kernel code under that protocol moved the raw owner from 711.0 to 417.2 GB/s on the same shape, so the sequential ratios were not measuring the kernel. Those rows are withdrawn rather than restated.

variant.header_loads: wide: d and scales_h as 4 u32 each, scales_l as 8 u32, extracted in registers (16 loads per lane per block instead of 24 mixed-width loads)
